newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Nov 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Nov 26.

text.p: General Motors Corp's Hughes Electronics Corp agreed to buy satellite-launching services from Rocket Systems, the Wall Street Journal reported.
- The Dow Jones industrial average ended higher than 6,500 points for the first time in weeks.
- Warren Buffett protested against the high commission fee that a firm charged to negotiate Gillette Co's purchase of Duracell.
- The television and computer industries agreed on the design of digital television sets.
- KeyCorp will close or sell 23 percent of its rural bank branches.
- Iraq might be able to export crude oil by the end of the year.
- Natural gas transportation companies saw their stock prices soar following the deal between Duke Power Co and PanEnergy Corp.
- Conrail Inc shareholders will vote next month on an amendment needed for its purchase by CSX Corp.
- Fidelity Investments and other U.S. financial firms are trying to export retirement plans like 401(k).
- Sales of existing U.S homes fell for the fifth straight month in October.
- The Food and Drug Administration approved Lilly Industries Inc's Prozac anti-depressant as a treatment for bulimia.
- The Supreme Court will hear a challenge to the taking of agricultural produce sales to pay for ad campaigns.
- Securities firms are expected to give out high year-end bonuses for investment bankers and traders.
- AnnTaylor Stores Corp named a veteran apparel retailer as president and chief operating officer.
- Campbell Soup Co unveiled a corporate reshuffling.
- U.S. bond prices closed a little higher in quiet trading without the momentum to equal the strong gains made by stocks.
- Applied Materials Inc has risen higher than stock investors had expected and market analysts project higher stock-price targets for the stock.
